value: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby first took notice when Obed Abernethy left town in his buggy.
unit: Mrs. Agatha Sowerby first took notice when Obed Abernethy left town in his buggy, later visiting Thirza Abernethy at Grey Shutters to express strong doubts upon learning he was adopting an orphan child. During a subsequent visit, she rudely mocked the young girl Nell's plain appearance and red hair, provoking an enraged outburst from Nell. Nell later visited her house to deliver a humble, dramatic apology, which Mrs. Sowerby accepted with forgiveness. When Nell later refused to return to school after an incident, Thirza sought advice from Mrs. Sowerby, who recommended allowing the girl to rest at home until her temper subsided. Obed eventually enlisted Mrs. Sowerby's help to buy fabric and sew a stylish new gown with puffed sleeves as a Christmas gift for Nell. Over time, Mrs. Sowerby's initial misgivings faded, leading her to compliment Nell's growth and grace.

label: History
value: Hugh Carrow spent three years in Alberta.
unit: Hugh Carrow spent three years in Alberta after his father fell ill. He also spent a summer visiting his cousins in New Brunswick before returning home. Upon attending Brierley school, Hugh teased Nell by calling her 'Carrots' and pulling her hair, causing an enraged Nell to smash her slate over his head. Hugh later engaged in an intense academic rivalry with Nell and silently competed with her in class while ignoring her. When Nell was stranded on a bridge pile after her boat sank, Hugh rescued her in his dory and offered her his friendship, though she stubbornly refused him. Later, both Hugh and Nell attended Regent's Academy together, where Hugh ultimately won the Medal while Nell won the Avery scholarship. Upon graduating, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application for the teaching position at the Brierley school so that Nell could take it instead to support her home. When Nell met him on the hill and thanked him for stepping aside, the former foes reconciled and became friends.

label: History
value: Isolde Pembroke received her name from a schoolmaster lodging at her home when she was born.
unit: Isolde Pembroke received her name from a schoolmaster lodging at her home when she was born, and she later learned a decorative crochet stitch while visiting her aunt in Delford. At Pear Hill, she met Nell Harcourt, and the two young girls quickly swore to be best friends forever. Though Isolde's mother ordered her to break off the friendship, leading to an emotional farewell, Isolde continued to exchange secret notes with Nell at Brierley school. When her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracted croup while their parents were away, Isolde rushed to Grey Shutters to seek help from Nell, who successfully treated the child. Isolde later hosted a party where Nell broke her ankle, and her family gave Nell slippers for Christmas that year.

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: “Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell."

label: Appearance
value: Nell has a slight frame.
unit: Nell possesses a slight, small, and slender frame, standing straight-backed and an inch taller than Isolde Pembroke. Her sharp, bright, and freckle-dusted face features a small pointed chin, a very pretty nose, and large, starry, earnest grey eyes. Her hair is famously red, described variously as ginger, fiery, crimson, auburn, Titian, or simply red, and is often worn in long braids or plaits. At times, her unplaited hair flows out like a radiant river, though on one occasion it mysteriously became green.

label: Personality
value: Nell is unusual.
unit: Nell is an unusual, intelligent, and compliant young girl who possesses an unselfish nature, though she is also known for a swift temper, an undesirable tendency to harbor animosity, and a resolute stubbornness. Intensely passionate in both her affections and her hatreds, she is remarkably talkative, theatrical in her phrasing, and relies heavily on a vivid imagination to pass the time. She frequently drifts into reveries during her chores and can be overly careless and hasty. Practically skilled, she is a fast runner, writes the finest essays about field afternoons, and has learned to bake cakes, despite otherwise being unable to cook. Her ambitions include passing her exams high to make Obed proud, qualifying for and preparing for the Entrance exam, becoming a teacher, and making Isolde Pembroke her closest companion. Furthermore, she desires to remain at Grey Shutters to care for Thirza Abernethy, even choosing to stay over attending Wexcombe College or accepting a scholarship.

label: History
value: Nell Harcourt was sent to live with Thirza and Obed Abernethy at Grey Shutters.
unit: An orphan girl, Nell Harcourt was sent to live with Thirza and Obed Abernethy at Grey Shutters, where Thirza and Obed ultimately decided to keep her despite an initial mix-up over her gender. Nell quickly formed a deep bond with Isolde Pembroke, though her hot temper occasionally caused trouble, such as when she smashed her slate over Hugh Carrow's head for teasing her about her red hair. She also inadvertently caused a stir by mistakenly serving currant wine to Isolde and later accidentally ruining a cake for the new minister with liniment. After a fall off a kitchen roof broke her ankle, Nell recovered and eventually attempted to dye her hair green, forcing Thirza to crop it short. Her adventurous nature led to another disaster when she acted out a story on a pond in a leaking boat, requiring Hugh Carrow to rescue her from the water. Nell later excelled academically under her teacher Miss Thorne, winning top marks on the island on her Regent's entrance exam and overcoming severe stage fright to deliver a lauded recitation at a charity concert. Following her move to Regent's Academy, Nell was devastated when Obed suddenly passed away after a bank failure. Learning that Thirza was losing her vision and faced with the prospect of selling Grey Shutters, Nell gave up her college scholarship to take a local teaching job at Brierley school to support Thirza. After discovering that Hugh Carrow had selflessly withdrawn his own application for the position so she could have it, Nell reconciled with him, contentedly accepting her new future at home.

Nell later excelled academically under her teacher Miss Thorne, winning top marks on the island on her Regent's entrance exam and overcoming severe stage fright to deliver a lauded recitation at a charity concert. Following her move to Regent's Academy, Nell was devastated when Obed suddenly passed away after a bank failure. Learning that Thirza was losing her vision and faced with the prospect of selling Grey Shutters, Nell gave up her college scholarship to take a local teaching job at Brierley school to support Thirza. After discovering that Hugh Carrow had selflessly withdrawn his own application for the position so she could have it, Nell reconciled with him, contentedly accepting her new future at home.

label: Personality
value: Obed Abernethy is quiet.
unit: Obed Abernethy is a quiet, bashful, and extremely shy individual who exhibits a remarkably timid nature. Taciturn and often silent, he rarely voices grievances or engages in full discussions, instead standing by as a patient, wise, and good-natured listener who appreciates loquacious companions. Despite his general bashfulness, he possesses a quiet stubbornness, clinging tenaciously to his own views once adopted. He harbors a deep-seated fear of little girls, as well as an aversion to women in general, excepting Thirza and Mrs. Agatha. Furthermore, he despises being surrounded by unfamiliar people or visiting places where he might be required to converse.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters
unit: Obed Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters alongside Thirza, having inherited the timid and bashful nature of his father. Wearing a thick, gentle brown beard since his twenties, he traveled to the train station expecting to collect an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to bring home an unexpected orphan girl named Nell instead. Although Thirza initially intended to send the child back, Obed harbored a quiet desire to keep her and offered the young girl his steady support. He secretly visited Nell in her room to persuade her to apologize to a neighbor after a outburst, and he later gifted her chocolates as Thirza's affection for the girl grew. Noticing how poorly Nell dressed compared to her friends, Obed made an awkward attempt to shop for stylish fabric and secured help to have a new Christmas gown made with fashionable puffed sleeves for her. He celebrated Nell's academic successes over the years, including her tying for first place on the island during her entrance examinations. In his old age, Obed suffered from significant heart trouble. After Nell achieved further success at Regent's Academy, news of a local bank failure caused Obed to collapse and die, leaving Grey Shutters in mourning.

label: History
value: Odette Pullen had a history of emotional dramatics.
unit: Odette Pullen had a history of emotional dramatics, weeping heavily during the departure of her schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon, despite having spent four weeks insisting she would be glad to see him go. She also nearly drowned while reaching far out for water lilies on the Lake of Glassy Waters, only saved when her sash was grabbed in time. In her youth, she participated in a dramatic play based on Tennyson's Elaine, playing the role of Guinevere. She was present during a reenactment of the tale alongside Isolde, and both girls experienced immense relief upon finding Nell alive after fearing she had drowned when her boat sank. Later, Odette and Barney Pullen picked up Nell and Isolde to escort them to the Pale Sands Hotel for a charity concert. Following the performance, Odette enjoyed supper with Nell and Isolde, and the group reflected cheerfully on the evening before departing together.

value: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny and pleasant disposition.
unit: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny and pleasant disposition, openly delighting in life, though she can also be sentimental and prone to hysteria. Additionally, she harbors a intense terror of plump green caterpillars and fears lying flat to feign death on a floating craft.

label: Personality
value: Thirza Abernethy is practical.
unit: Thirza Abernethy is a practical, rational, and composed individual who maintains a stern demeanor and an unyielding sense of morality. Though Thirza initially insisted that Nell be returned, she reconsidered after visiting a local woman and agreed to keep her, taking on the responsibility of giving the girl a religious upbringing. Thirza proved to be a strict authority figure, scolding Nell's frequent outbursts, demanding formal apologies when Nell behaved disrespectfully, and restricting her from wearing flowers to church. However, Thirza slowly softened toward the child; when an amethyst brooch went missing, Thirza mistakenly accused Nell of stealing it, but upon discovering it caught in her own shawl, she felt deep remorse and forgave Nell's fabricated confession. Over the following years, Thirza supervised Nell's education, allowing her to study at home during difficult times, providing permission for town trips, and eventually supporting her enrollment in entrance exam preparation. After Nell earned top marks and attended Regent's Academy, Thirza shared the tragic news of a bank failure that precipitated the sudden collapse and death of her brother, Obed. Devastated by the loss, Thirza soon learned from an eye doctor that her vision was severely failing, leaving her considering the sale of Grey Shutters until Nell relinquished a college scholarship to stay home and care for her.

value: Thirza Abernethy said: "No. A boy is what we need to assist Obed on the farm. To us, a girl would be useless. Remove your hat. On the hall table, I’ll place it along with your bag."

value: Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

On Christmas morning, Nell receives the gown at Grey Shutters and is overwhelmed with joy and gratitude.

value: Thirza attends a political rally in town
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
value: Isolde Pembroke hosts a party.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pembroke carries her home to Thirza Abernethy, and Nell spends the next seven weeks recovering in bed while friends, neighbors, and local figures visit her.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

Thirza later finds Nell weeping dramatically over the imagined future heartbreak of Isolde marrying and leaving her, which moves Thirza to rare, genuine laughter.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
value: Thirza attends a political rally in town
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

value: Thirza attends a political rally in town
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

label: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

unit: Thirza presents Nell with three simple dresses and refuses her request for fashionable puffed sleeves, sending her off to study Sunday school materials. label: CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong
value: Nell is in her room at Grey Shutters.
chapter: CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong
unit: In her room at Grey Shutters, Nell reflects on her first year with Thirza, who admits she does not regret keeping her. When Thirza asks her to fetch an apron pattern from the Pembrokes, Nell confesses that she and Isolde invented ghosts in the nearby wood, making her terrified to cross it in the dark. Unmoved, Thirza forces Nell to walk through the woods to teach her a lesson, and Nell reluctantly completes the frightening errand.
